name: near-membrane-fields
title: Fields next to a curved membrane: native VCell on pyvcell's smoothed grid vs co-sim on a body-fitted mesh

question:
B2b found that the native hybrid loses molecules at the curved membrane. Where does that
show up in the field, and does the co-simulation have its own boundary artifact?
Native fields are read on pyvcell's smoothed unstructured grid, so boundary elements sit
near the true membrane rather than on the staircase.
hypothesis:
With A placed uniformly in the ball, A stays uniform in expectation, so E[B] is spatially
uniform. Any radial structure in the ensemble-mean B therefore comes from particle-to-field
transfer at the membrane.
- Native: exterior-node binning drops B sources next to the membrane, so the outer shell
  should be depleted.
- Co-sim: exterior-node counts are folded onto boundary DOFs (Pᵀ), so its outer shell
  should be slightly enriched. Study B2d later revised this cause; see the conclusion.
objective:
Same ball, grid, mesh and solvers as B2b. Conversion A_p → B_f (k = 0.5 /s, 20,000 A
uniform in the ball), t = 2 s, 32 seeds per solver.
- E[B] = A₀(1 − e^(−kt))/(V·N_A), with V each solver's own domain volume.
- The interior is r < R/2. The outer shell is r > R − 2Δ = 3.5 µm.
- Native values are volume-weighted on the smoothed cells; co-sim values are weighted by
  the lumped mass of the P1 DOFs.
description:
New helper: viva_pde_particle.reference.vcell_vtk.smoothed_domain builds pyvcell's smoothed
grid (from_mesh3d_volume → get_volume_vtk_grid → smooth_unstructured_grid_surface) from a
native .mesh file and maps node data onto its cells by global index.

Finding on the exporter: pyvcell and VCell's Java exporter (vis CartesianMesh.getVolumeElementBox)
draw element i as [i·L/N, (i+1)·L/N]. vcell-fvsolver's mesh is node-centred (node i at
i·L/(N−1)). On this 37³ mesh the exported cell domain is 8.4% smaller than the ball, and
elements are shifted by up to ~0.1 µm. smoothed_domain maps the corners onto node-centred
voxels before smoothing (node_centred=True). That is an analysis-side correction;
pyvcell itself is unchanged.

The mean native field on the smoothed grid is written to results/native_mean_B_smoothed.vtu
(open it in ParaView).

conclusion:
Results (results/metrics.json, 2026-10-03; 32 seeds per solver; co-sim re-run with the B2d default membrane):

**Geometry.**
- The node-centred smoothed cell domain is within −0.50% of the ball volume. Taken as-is,
  the pyvcell export is −8.4% (the tiling convention above).
- Smoothing cuts the RMS radial error of the boundary surface from 0.108 to 0.065 µm.

**Interior.** Both solvers match the exact uniform E[B]: native +0.49%, co-sim −0.37%.

**Next to the membrane.**
- **Native:**
  - The outer shell (r > 3.5 µm) is 2.3% below the interior (z = −20).
  - The profile declines smoothly from about r = 2.5 µm to 0.98 at the membrane: the
    diffusive footprint of the B sources dropped at the boundary.
  - This is B2b's exterior-binning loss, now localized.
- **Co-sim:**
  - The shell is +0.12% (z = 1.2), unbiased.
  - The first run, with Smoldyn confined by the exact sphere, gave +1.3% (z = 10).
    This study attributed that to Pᵀ folding of exterior-node counts. Study B2d showed the
    cause was the domain mismatch instead: particles in the ~1.4% sliver between sphere and
    inscribed mesh load the boundary DOFs.
  - Confining Smoldyn by the mesh's own boundary (now the default) removes it.
- **Smoothing** barely changes the native shell bias (−2.27% vs −2.29% on the staircase).
  The field is smooth on the scale of the boundary displacement (< 0.1 µm), so the smoothed
  grid helps geometry and visualization; the field artifact is in the coupling.

Neither effect is a limitation of VCell's geometry or PDE numerics. Both come from how
particles near a curved membrane are binned to the field.
- Native: VCellSmoldynOutput::computeHistogram (vcell-fvsolver,
  bridgeVCellSmoldyn/VCellSmoldynOutput.cpp:476–548) bins each molecule to the nearest
  node. Its correction for a nearest node in a different compartment (re-bin to the
  nearest same-compartment neighbour) is present but commented out. Re-enabling it is the
  likely native fix (virtualcell/vcell-fvsolver#25).
- Co-sim fix (B2d, done): the mesh boundary as the particle membrane.

findings.statement: The node-centred smoothed cell domain reproduces the ball to within −0.50% (b2c_node_centred_smoothed_volume_rel_err = −0.0050), against −8.4% for the pyvcell export taken as-is, and smoothing cuts the RMS radial error of the boundary surface from 0.108 µm (staircase) to 0.065 µm.
findings.next_action: None — the analysis-side node-centred tiling correction recovers the geometry.

findings.statement: Away from the membrane both solvers match the exact uniform E[B]: the native interior is +0.49% (b2c_native_interior_rel = 0.0049) and the co-sim interior +0.25% (b2c_cosim_interior_rel = 0.0025), both well inside ±2%.
findings.next_action: None — interior transfer is unbiased on both solvers.

findings.statement: The native outer shell (r > 3.5 µm) sits 2.3% below the interior (b2c_native_shell_bias = −0.0227, z = −20.1), failing the ±1% unbiasedness band, while the co-sim shell is unbiased at +0.12% (b2c_cosim_shell_bias = 0.0012, z = 1.17). This localizes B2b's exterior-binning loss to the field next to the curved membrane: molecules binned to nodes outside the voxelized cell drop their PDE source. The native fix is to re-enable the commented-out same-compartment binning correction in VCellSmoldynOutput::computeHistogram (virtualcell/vcell-fvsolver#25).
findings.next_action: Re-enable the same-compartment binning correction in vcell-fvsolver and re-run the shell bias.

regression_compatibility.basis: results/metrics.json is committed and regenerated by sims/run.py; the four geometry and interior tests pass, and the native-shell failure is a pinned, intentional marker of the boundary artifact.

biological_validation.basis: Both solvers reproduce the exact uniform E[B] in the interior (native +0.49%, co-sim +0.25%); the only departure is the native near-membrane depletion.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-03 localizes B2b's native mass loss to exterior-node binning at the curved membrane (−2.3% outer-shell depletion), distinguishing it from the co-sim, whose shell is unbiased once the mesh boundary is the particle membrane (B2d).

conclusion_logic.if_primary_tests_pass: Both solvers transfer particles to the field without interior bias and the smoothed grid represents the ball — the near-membrane depletion seen natively is a coupling artifact, not a PDE or geometry error. Pursue the vcell-fvsolver same-compartment binning fix.
conclusion_logic.if_primary_tests_fail: An interior bias beyond ±2% or a smoothed-grid volume error beyond ±1% would mean the particle-to-field transfer or the geometry correction is wrong — re-examine smoothed_domain and the lumped-mass weighting before trusting the shell diagnosis.

report.caveat: The native-shell test fails by design (−2.3%) to keep the boundary artifact visible; it marks an open vcell-fvsolver issue, not a study defect. Native fields need the dev pixi env.

rerun.note: Ball conversion, 32 seeds per solver; the native arm reads fields on pyvcell's smoothed grid and needs the dev pixi env (pyvcell spatial-hybrid).
